text:
mina: FYI ran into a weird combo on NixOS + snapd. installed redwoodctl via snap for a dev VM, then tried to `redwoodctl auth login` and `redwoodctl localtest` and they each read different config stores. auth wrote token to /root/snap/redwoodctl/common/.config/redwood but localtest (run by my user) looked in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME and then the system snap mount path and failed with "no credentials". anyone hit snap confinement + config path mismatch?

hiro: snap pretty much isolates per-snap data under /root or per-user snap dirs. did you install as root or via `--classic`? snapcraft can be funky about $HOME.

mina: I used `sudo snap install redwoodctl --beta` because snap said I needed classic and the package didn't set --classic in the store. installer seemed to run as root.

ops-bot: Note: snap installs may create both /root/snap/... and /home/<user>/snap/... depending on how it was invoked. See https://snapcraft.io/docs/snap-userdata for details.

felix: hmm two problems here: 1) installer running as root writing token to root-owned snap common dir, 2) CLI run from user session looking in user XDG paths. We should make the CLI check snap common/store locations as fallback and prefer per-user snap dir when run as user.

mina: repro steps:
```
sudo snap install redwoodctl --beta
sudo redwoodctl auth login --token-file /root/.redwood-token
# then as user
redwoodctl localtest --profile=dev
# error: no credentials
```

felix: easy workaround: `sudo snap run --shell redwoodctl` to drop installer into same confinement as the user snap or re-run the login without sudo. But that's not great for automated installs.

hiro: another wrinkle: on NixOS, people often manage packages as system scripts. If the package manager runs the post-install as root, it will seed config at root. CLI should look for tokens in this order: $REDWOOD_CONFIG, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME, /var/lib/redwood/token, snap common dir (/var/snap/redwoodctl/common/.config/redwood), and snap root dir (/root/snap/...). Also detect when UID!=EUID or when running under sudo and warn.

mina: also saw auth retry behavior: after token rotate, localtest kept retrying auth every 10s and produced a flood of logs in our dev cluster. it didn't exponential backoff, just hammer. was that intended? it makes CI flaky.

ci: CI note: nightly image build failed due to repeated auth retries causing rate-limit hits on hosted auth. Logged as flake #578.

felix: that retry behavior is definitely a bug. We should implement jitter + exponential backoff with max cap and a clearer error message after N attempts (e.g., "temporary auth error: will retry in 30s (attempt 4/8)"). I'll open a PR for backoff + logs.

hiro: suggestion for installer: if installing system-wide, write a machine-scoped profile in /etc/redwood/profile.json with metadata indicating origin (snap/systemd/nix). CLI can show `redwoodctl config sources` to help users debug where the token came from.

mina: made a small script to migrate root token to user profile for now:
```
sudo cp /root/snap/redwoodctl/common/.config/redwood/token.json $HOME/.config/redwood/token.json
sudo chown $(id -u):$(id -g) $HOME/.config/redwood/token.json
```
worked locally.

felix: filed issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/612 - title: "snap/nix install path mismatch and noisy auth retry; add snap common dir and backoff". added repro and suggested order of checks + backoff change.

mina: thanks — this unblocks our Nix dev images. leaving a note in our infra image build to avoid sudoing the login step or to run the migration script as part of post-install. :white_check_mark:
